## History

Phillips secured his position as a school teacher through the influence of his uncle, who served as a trustee. During a school day, he punished [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) for smashing her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head by making her stand in front of the class. Phillips later punished [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) again by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert, which prompted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to temporarily quit attending school.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P3](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P33](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P38](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0038), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Relationships

### [Prissy Andrews](../character/prissy-andrews.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/phillips--prissy-andrews.md)

Mr. Phillips has a romantic involvement with [Prissy Andrews](../character/prissy-andrews.md). As part of this affection, he has given her Mayflowers alongside the sentiment 'sweets to the sweet'.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001)_
